summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for dehydration due to four days of non-bloody diarrhea, preceded by abdominal cramping. She presented with signs of dehydration including dry mouth, chills, and fatigue. She was started on IV fluids and kept NPO initially for bowel rest. A stool test for C. difficile returned negative, but given her history of C. diff and small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, she was treated with a course of metronidazole. Her tube feeds were resumed and advanced successfully, with good tolerance. Enteral nutrition was provided to support recovery. Her symptoms resolved, and she was discharged home on a regimen including metronidazole, pantoprazole, prochlorperazine as needed, and her baseline psychiatric and hypoglycemia medications. Follow-up with her bariatric team was recommended.
